title: Illustration / Characters / Mouths
slide_intent: Allow controlled asymmetry in a mouth so a simple character can communicate a more lifelike emotion.
strategic_value: A varied mouth family can help Duolingo expand expression while retaining the same basic head construction.
demonstration: Twelve faces in four rows compare mouths of different shapes, sizes and positions, accompanied by a note about asymmetry.
practical_value: Try a mouth that favors one side when a symmetrical treatment feels emotionally flat.

content_islands.name: Mouth-expression grid
content_islands.spec: Arrange twelve repeated head shapes in three columns at left, varying the mouth while retaining a comparable facial framework.

content_islands.name: Asymmetry rationale
content_islands.spec: Place the Mouths heading and explanation at right, connecting less geometric forms with emotion.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text says asymmetry is more lifelike and brings more emotion to the face.
reference_purposes.Expression: The grid demonstrates varied expressive mouth shapes.
reference_purposes.Application: The examples show how mouth position and shape change the same simple face.

ingredient.name: Asymmetric mouths
ingredient.role: Give a simple face a stronger emotional reading.
ingredient.application: Allow mouth shapes to favor one side and use less rigid geometry when it serves expression.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. The source says most mouths favor one side; it does not require asymmetry in every mouth.
